en.title: Minimum Cost to Move Within a Grid
en.description:
In a rectangular grid you can only move up, down, left or right. Crossing between rows i and i+1 in any column costs costRows[i]; crossing between columns j and j+1 in any row costs costCols[j]. Find the minimum total cost from the start to the destination. The statement gives no obstacle positions, so this site interprets the whole grid as passable.

See the statement/review record for the problem source and the basis of the rules; limits marked in the input ranges are supplements added by this site.
en.input: The first line contains rows cols initR initC finalR finalC, with 0-based coordinates; the second line contains rows−1 costs between rows; the third line contains cols−1 costs between columns. Original: 1≤rows,cols≤100000, coordinates are valid, and 0≤(cost of each edge)≤10000.
en.explanation: Process the input according to the problem rules; see the companion notes for the full approach, the correctness argument and the complexity.
hints: Changing the row coordinate must cross every row edge between initR and finalR, and likewise for columns; compute the cost sum of each of these two stretches and add them.
